newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines seen buying wheat on price dips -trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seen buying wheat on price dips -trade.

text.p: Philippine grain importers are expected to return to the market next week to buy up to 50,000 tonnes of wheat on price dips, traders in Manila said on Friday.
"I expect Philippine flour millers to buy at least 50,000 tonnes of wheat for their April requirements," a senior trader for a Manila-based commodity house said.

A flour company on Wednesday bought 5,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 14 percent protein, and another 5,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat at 13.5 percent at an average price of US$189 a tonne FOB U.S. Pacific Northwest (PNW) for April shipment.
Dealers said this company plans to buy an additional 15,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, while another firm will probably be in for 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for its April requirements.
Philippine grain importers were fairly active this week, with two Philippine flour firms buying 40,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Japan's Mitsubishi Corp.
The two firms bought 13,750 tonnes of western white wheat at about $157-$158 a tonne FOB U.S. PNW, dealers said.

They also bought 12,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 13 percent protein, at $183 to $184 a tonne FOB PNW and 14,250 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 14 percent, at $186 to $187 a tonne FOB PNW.
Prices of hard flour were quoted unchanged at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag while soft flour was seen steady at 260 pesos per 25-kg bag.
The official National Food Authority (NFA) is expected to remain on the sidelines in the coming week after its recent rice-buying spree although it may re-enter the corn market soon.
The state-run grains body recently purchased 205,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand, 200,000 tonnes from Vietnam, 150,000 tonnes from China and 100,000 tonnes from Malaysia.
The imported rice is expected to arrive before July and ahead of the seasonally lean third quarter when supplies of the staple food of the country's 70 million people becomes tight.

The NFA said the nation's total rice stocks, as of March 4, amounted to 1.75 million tonnes, against 1.487 million tonnes in the same period last year. The Philippines' daily rice consumption reaches 22,000 tonnes.
Importers were also awaiting the arrival next week of 120,000 tonnes of corn bought from China by the NFA, which is expected to re-enter the corn market after delivery of the staple.
An Agriculture Department official said local hog raisers have asked the NFA to import an additional 300,000 tonnes of corn, which is used mainly in the Philippines for animal feed.
The average retail price of yellow corn rose to 10.68 pesos a kg from last week's 10.62 pesos while the price of white corn also increased to 10.95 pesos a kg from 10.91 pesos.
